newsitem.title: UK: THE PROTEUS COLUMN - Japan insurance rates, merger.
newsitem.headline: THE PROTEUS COLUMN - Japan insurance rates, merger.

text.p: Indications from Japan suggest that foreign non-life insurance companies are getting together to change the process of calculating insurance rate tariffs.

Currently these rates are calculated by a range of special entities such as the Fire and Marine Insurance Rating Association of Japan. But there is increasing support among foreign insurers for the creation of a single listed company which would centralise these operations. On addition it could offer a central database on claims payments to reduce fraud and a consultancy service to help plan new products.

Reform of the insurance ratings bodies was one of the issues agreed on in the accord which ended the dispute between Japan and the US over insurance deregulation, and that is what is giving momentum to the new proposal.

But reform in Japan is never easy, and doubtless supporters of the single rate calculation company will be planning how they can persuade the Japanese insurance industry complex to go along with it without starting another long term dispute.

Merger activity and speculation continues to sweep the insurance market. Yesterday saw the merger of US Life with American General in the biggest financial transaction in American history. No doubt the two companies were helped in reaching a pact by the long relationship between Crosby and American General Chairman Harold Hook, who was a top executive at US Life before leaving in 1970.

In the UK, Willis Corroon Chairman Max Taylor is saying he is not convinced it will do his company well to be involved in a merger. He says he is sceptical about the benefits and happy with his own plan for growing the business. However few market observers are taking his comments to be an indication that Willis will not do a merger.
